Description: A clay bulla found in 2008 by Eilat Mazar in the City of David (Area G), in the same strata and a few yards from the Jehucal bulla, reading 'Gedaliah son of Pashhur'. Gedaliah son of Pashhur is named in Jeremiah 38:1 among the princes who sought Jeremiah's death for preaching surrender to Babylon, and his family is tied to Jeremiah 20, where Pashhur son of Immer, chief officer of the Temple, had Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks.
Interpretations: Like the Jehucal bulla found beside it, this is a direct match to Jeremiah 38: the seal of a named opponent of Jeremiah, from the same Jerusalem strata and the same final generation of Judah. The pair of bullae together corroborate the court's cast of characters in Jeremiah's last years.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile
BiblicalSignificance: The seal of a second prince named in Jeremiah 38:1 survives from Zedekiah's Jerusalem, confirming the Bible's account of the officials who moved against Jeremiah.
